items.review_rationale: Read uniform convergence on real domain by one epsilon-dependent threshold independent of all points, contrasting pointwise thresholds and retaining real absolute-value metric.

references.phrase: metric uniform convergence specialized to real line

references.context: For each positive ε a single natural number Nε works for all domain inputs x and all indices n≥Nε.

references.disposition: This is strictly stronger than pointwise convergence except in special cases.

items.review_rationale: Read countable mutual independence of measurable random variables via their generated sigma algebras, with common measurable codomain and joint probability space.

references.context: Collection of all measurable preimages X_n^{-1}(B) for events B in codomain sigma-algebra.
Each X_n has the same set S with measurable sigma-algebra Sigma_S.

references.disposition: Definition makes sigma-algebra independence primary, rather than pairwise independence of random variables.

items.review_rationale: Read mutual independence of countably many sub-sigma-algebras through factorization for all finite distinct index selections and arbitrary events chosen from each selected algebra.

references.phrase: pair of independent sigma algebras special case
finite selection of pairwise distinct indices
references.context: For each m≥1 choose indices i_1,…,i_m with no repetitions.
Joint probability of intersecting any selected measurable events equals product of their individual probabilities.

references.phrase: mutual independence is stronger than pairwise
references.disposition: Factorization required for arbitrary finite index selections, not only m=2.

items.review_rationale: Read independence of two sub-sigma-algebras as probability factorization for every choice of one event from each, preserving distinction from independence of the algebras as sets.

references.context: P(A intersect B) equals P(A)P(B) for all events A in G1 and B in G2.

references.disposition: Requires all event pairs, not existence of some independent pair.
